status: source reviewed; two findings corrected by inspection; native execution not evaluated
scope: native screenshot runner supervision and evidence binding
shared Cargo executable selection and offline caller

source_state.identity_basis: exact reviewed file fingerprints; no clean-build or full-tree acceptance claim

findings.trigger: Cargo, a build script, or dependency acquisition stalls or emits excessive output.
findings.original_effect: Command::output buffered build output and had no deadline; an outer CI timeout could terminate the job before build logs or a result report were written. Fixture log limits only applied to reads after process exit.
findings.correction: Fresh private log files are opened before spawn. Cargo and each fixture use an owned Unix process group. The polling supervisor stops the group on deadline or sampled log-size excess and waits for the direct child. Build failure reaches the common failed-report path.

findings.trigger: A fixture is stopped because a log exceeds the sampled byte limit, then bounded_read rejects that oversized log.
findings.original_effect: The failed row retained the byte-limit error but discarded its already-known exit code and stop reason. Raw logs remained and the run could not pass.
findings.correction: A partial failed row records exit_code and stop_reason immediately after wait; later read or receipt errors augment it.

static_checks: Cargo JSON parser accepts only an executable for the requested target name and rejects missing, malformed or duplicate executable artifacts. Both GUI and offline CLI callers use it, preserving Cargo-reported custom target-directory paths.
Each fixture receipt must be unique and match its fixture and canonical output path. Scale values must be finite and positive; its dimensions must match decoded PNG dimensions.
PNG content is read once into a byte-limited buffer; signature, bounded dimensions, decoding and SHA-256 all use that same immutable buffer.
Source and executable hashes are checked at both endpoints. Initial identity failures prevent execution; late identity errors prevent a passed report while preserving accumulated rows.

Build and fixture failures reach the report path, including termination metadata after the last correction. Raw artifacts remain. Existing report and export targets are protected by no-clobber publication.

The binary export helper preserves the existing private atomic export behavior: create_new temporary file, complete write and sync, then hard-link publication without replacement and temporary-file cleanup.

The workflow runs on macOS with read-only repository permissions and always uploads the artifact directory. Report limitations correctly restrict this to primary-viewport fixture smoke and exclude visual parity, child windows, capture, focus, AX, installation and inference.

external_test_evidence.evaluator_action: read retained log and verify its hash and summary only
external_test_evidence.source_binding_limit: The retained run002 log predates the final partial-termination-row correction. No final-workspace or final-source executed-test result is asserted here.

limitations: Static review plus inspection of an implementer-executed unit log; no actual native API, GUI, screenshot runner, GPU readback or CI job was executed by the evaluator.
Log limits are sampled every 25 milliseconds and can be exceeded between samples. These are not strict on-disk byte caps.
Process-group supervision covers the owned group and reaps the direct child; it is not a sandbox or a guarantee about detached descendants.
Endpoint fingerprints do not continuously monitor source, executable or output-file replacement.
A valid receipt and PNG establish capture-smoke evidence only; they do not establish pixel-content correctness, matched reference parity or model quality.
This proposal does not claim a final coordinated workspace test pass. Prior failed and blocked reports remain unchanged.
